item.title: Will Game 6 be Valkyries' breakfast of champions? Here are the key factors
item.description: Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams moves the ball while defended by Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese during Game 5 of the WNBA Finals on Monday at Chase Center. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle) The Golden State Valkyries have shot to clinch the WNBA championship Thursday in Atlanta. If this team can fend off the Atlanta Dream once more, fans watching on the West Coast may be polishing off their morning cup of coffee and toast by the time Valkyries players are hoisting the trophy. Such is the reality of a 12:30 p.m. ET tipoff in Atlanta, the compromise WNBA took to ensure that Game 6 would be played at State Farm Arena in front of 17,000 fans instead of the 3,500 at the Dream's typical home at Gateway Center Arena at College Park. For the Valkyries and their fans in California, that means the most important game of the year will start while the morning grogginess is wearing off. The strange schedule means less time to rest and recover between Game 5, which the Valkyries won 64-55 on Monday, and neither team will get a shootaround or walk-through. Thursday's game is do-or-die. The Valkyries have no interest in trying to win a title in a decisive Game 7 on their home court, while the Dream will be fighting for a chance to get back to San Francisco. "As much as we love Ballhalla, we don't want to come back here," center Kiah Stokes said. "We need to go in with the mentality that we have to win." Dream star Angel Reese might have set the tone for Game 6 with her frustrated comments after Game 5. She called out the officiating, saying there was a clear shift when Atlanta took a 2-1 series lead that allowed Golden State to get more physical without getting called for fouls. "I'm still trying to figure out how to play through the physicality," Reese said. "A lot of us are getting fouled and they're not calling it. Or we're talking to the ref after and they're saying, ‘Oh, we'll get you next time.' So it is a little frustrating, especially in the moment of it. … We'll figure it out, we'll just have to continue to push through the physicality and hopefully it goes our way the next game." With Reese having spoken up - and Dream head coach Karl Smesko backed her up - will the whistle be quicker in Game 6? After their Game 4 win, Valkyries star Gabby Williams said Golden State's big adjustment was not to wait for the whistle and lean in on the physicality these stakes typically present. Head coach Natalie Nakase echoed that after Reese's comments. "It's the Finals. This is it. Both teams really want to win this," Nakase said, asked about the physicality. "These are two defensive-minded teams … they like physicality, so that's part of it. You guys act like I'm shocked, I ain't shocked about this. You have an Atlanta Dream team that's well-coached, that has dogs, same as us. It's part of it." Statistically, the officiating has heavily favored the Dream throughout this series. They've taken 130 free throws compared to the Valkyries' 78. Trips to the line

item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL - OCTOBER 26: Garrett Mitchell #5 of the Milwaukee Brewers celebrates with William Contreras #24 after scoring in the fifth inning during Game Three of the 2026 World Series presented by Capital One between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on Monday, October 26, 2026 in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Tonight could see the great city of Milwaukee inundated in a collective inebriation not seen in decades. Their mighty Brewers sit on the cusp of a World Series title after seizing a commanding 3-0 lead over their rivals the Tampa Bay Rays, the latter of whom now must achieve the impossible if they’re to hang their first banner in Tropicana Field. The Rays will at least have their home field on which to lean in Game 4, as the Trop will again be the host site for the action. That was anything but a good thing for Tampa in Game 3, however, as the Brewers hitting machine sliced and carved them to pieces in a 10-1 rout that sent the Rays to the brink. All hands will obviously be on-deck for Tampa in what could end up being the final Major League Baseball game played for awhile, what with the December 1st expiration of the Collective Bargaining Agreement and the looming lockout from owners on the docket. Griffin Jax will be tasked with the start, though Tampa will obviously have a quick hook if need be – something that yesterday’s drubbing exacerbated as they needed to turn away from starter Freddy Peralta earlier than anyone had hoped. Dustin May will toe the rubber for Milwaukee as they look to clinch. First pitch is set for just after 8:00 PM ET, with coverage once again on FOX. item.title: Mikel Arteta remains tight-lipped on Max Dowman reaction after 16-year-old’s red card
item.description: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta refused to provide further explanation to his angry reaction to Max Dowman ’s red card in the Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town. But Arteta revealed what he said to Dowman as he walked off the pitch was to do with “something we discussed already before the match”. Arteta appeared to have harsh words for the the 16-year-old Arsenal prodigy following the first red card of his senior career, which came as the Gunners lost on penalties. Arteta appeared angered by Dowman’s red card (Getty) Dowman was making his second start of the season for Arsenal after his stunning two-goal against Ipswich in the previous round of the competition. But Fleetwood made Arsenal’s night a frustrating one and the League Two side were hanging on for penalties when Dowman was sent off in the 85th minute. The teeanger was on the receiving end of a heavy challenge from behind from the Fleetwood midfielder Harrison Neal, who lunged at him from behind near the touchline. Dowman kicked out at Neal in response to his tackle, sparking a brawl between the teams as the Fleetwood players reacted angrily to his retaliation. The referee Michael Salisbury, who did not have VAR available, showed Dowman a straight-red card for violent conduct, leaving Arsenal down to 10 men. And there looked to be an furious reaction from Arteta towards Dowman as he walked off the pitch and went straight down the tunnel. The incident took place on the opposite side of the pitch to Arteta’s dugout but the manager appeared to have sharp words for Dowman as he left the pitch. Dowman was sent off on his second start of the season (Reuters) Arteta said he still had to watch the incident back before commenting on it, but it was notable that he had no comforting words of support for the forward. “It's difficult to see on the cameras like that so I'd prefer to watch it back properly so I can assess the situation,” he told Sky Sports. Asked if the 16-year-old can learn from the red card because of his young age, Arteta replied: “Yeah, we all learn from everything, yeah.” Then asked what he said to Dowman when he left the pitch, Arteta told BBC Radio 5 Live: “Something that we discussed already before the match.” Dowman will now be suspended for Arsenal’s next three Premier League games, starting with Sunday’s trip to Liverpool. It comes as Arteta is expected to be without his first-choice right winger, Bukayo Saka, due to injury for the next few weeks. And Arteta also revealed that his second-choice right winger Noni Madueke could be unavailable against Liverpool due to injury. It suggests Dowman could have been in line to start for Arsenal at Liverpool prior to his sending off at Fleetwood.

item.title: John Smoltz changes tune on Brewers star William Contreras’ ABS challenges, but there’s 1 problem
item.description: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images John Smoltz changes tune on Brewers star William Contreras’ ABS challenges, but there’s 1 problem appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Former MLB star pitcher and current broadcaster John Smoltz received some backlash for comments he made during Game 3 of the World Series between the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays on Monday. Smoltz questioned Brewers catcher William Contreras’ decision to challenge a ball in a 2-0 game. Contreras has been exceptional when it comes to ABS challenges, and he even got the call that Smoltz questioned correct. Smoltz’s issue wasn’t with the specific pitch Contreras challenged. Rather, the Hall of Famer felt it wasn’t the proper time to challenge it. Many fans felt it was a fine time to challenge it since the score was only 2-0. Smoltz addressed his comments on Tuesday during an appearance on MLB Network’s MLB Now. While Smoltz changed his tune on the situation, he failed to acknowledge the score of the game element, instead claiming it was 10-0. Perhaps he was thinking of a different situation, but his comments did not directly address fans’ complaints. Not only has he been elite at using his ABS challenges, but he’s blocking seemingly every pitch, throwing runners out, and producing quality at-bats. He could win the World Series MVP. item.title: UConn's Dan Hurley ranked No. 1 college basketball coach by CBS Sports for third straight year
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - MARCH 14: Head coach's Dan Hurley of the Connecticut Huskies and Rick Pitino of the St. John's Red Storm shake hands looks on before the2026 Big East Men's Tournament Championship game at Madison Square Garden on March 14, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) (Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) Dan Hurley saw off many of college basketball's best coaches to reach the 2026 national championship game, ousting Mick Cronin, Tom Izzo, Jon Scheyer, and Brad Underwood before falling to Michigan in Indianapolis. The UConn men's basketball coach has reestablished the Huskies as a premier college basketball contender after a down 2024-25 season, and with Michigan coach Dusty May leaving for the NBA, CBS Sports has once again ranked Hurley as the sport's best coach entering the 2026-27 campaign, making this his third straight year atop the rankings. "Hurley guided UConn to its third national title game appearance in a four-year span before the Huskies ran into a historically dominant Michigan team on the season's final night," CBS Sports writes. "While Hurley fell just short of becoming the first coach since John Wooden to win three national championships in four years, he's presiding over a dynasty. At 53, he could keep it going for quite some time. He was the unanimous No. 1 choice by our panelists." Hurley will share the sideline with many of his chief rivals on CBS Sports' list after assembling likely the most difficult nonconference schedule in program history. After preseason exhibitions against (No. 5) Matt Painter's Purdue and (No. 7) Izzo's Michigan State, the Huskies will hit the road for blockbuster matchups against No. 6 Tommy Lloyd and Arizona, No. 9 Scheyer and Duke, No. 12 Underwood and Illinois and No. 22 Ryan Odom and Virginia - meanwhile, No. 8 Bill Self and Kansas will come to Connecticut in December. The only other Big East coach featured in CBS Sports' rankings is St. John's coach Rick Pitino, who ranks No. 3. The publication notes that Pitino has won consecutive Big East regular-season and conference-tournament championships, but lacks the same success in NCAA Tournament play. Eight seasons into his UConn tenure, Hurley hasn't matched the lofty win totals of some peers at the top of CBS Sports' list, but the New Jersey native is already one of just three active coaches to win multiple national championships. Over the past four seasons, Hurley has reached three Final Fours, while no other coach in the sport has made multiple trips. Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. item.title: IRSC tables vote to cut historic swim, dive dynasty
item.description: OKEECHOBEE — A decades-long dynasty unmatched across collegiate athletics remains alive — for now. The greatest threat to the dynasty built by the Indian River State College swimming and diving teams doesn't come from a rival college or program trying to knock it off its perch. It comes from IRSC's administration and its belief that the best way for the institution to prosper financially is to move forward without it. The hot-button topic was the chief item on the agenda during Indian River State College's latest Board of Trustees meeting on Tuesday, Oct. 27, as current and former swimmers and divers, along with parents and supporters of the program, filled the Williamson Conference Center Auditorium at the Dixon Hendry Campus in Okeechobee. After hours of discussion among board members and roughly two dozen people offering public comment, the topic was tabled until Nov. 17, the date of the next board meeting. IRSC President Dr. Tim Moore and Athletic Director Scott Kimmerman were asked to return with a comprehensive financial report on the program, as well as input from the community. More: IRSC proposes eliminating championship swim, dive programs More: Petition to save IRSC swim, dive programs at almost 10,000 signatures The report will be posted on the school's website one week before the meeting. If a vote to eliminate the program had been approved Tuesday, the move would have taken effect at the start of the 2027-28 academic year. "I'm very grateful that everyone on the board heard us and gave us a chance to speak about the situation," said Grace Hanson, a former IRSC swimmer who helped the program win NJCAA national championships in 2022 and 2023. "We're very grateful that they're considering delaying or tabling the vote. We really want to keep the swim team. We feel like it benefits Indian River State College, and we just want to do whatever it takes to help them see that." Indian River State's men's team has won 52 consecutive NJCAA national championships, while the women's team has captured 48 straight national titles. The transition of the school's softball, men's basketball and baseball programs to NJCAA Division II, where IRSC's volleyball team currently competes, was also on the meeting's agenda. The college would no longer cover student-athletes' meal plans, room and board if those programs moved to Division II. Additionally, the administration will evaluate whether it is feasible to reinstate women's basketball for the 2028-29 academic year, two years after the college eliminated the sport in 2024. Those discussions were also tabled. 'We have an imbalance' Moore began his opening statement Tuesday by thanking the community for attending the meeting while explaining that serving as IRSC president is a "tough job." He later said that while he appreciates the success the swim and dive teams have enjoyed, he believes maintaining the program in its current form is unsustainable. item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 24: Head coach Kenny Atkinson of the Cleveland Cavaliers talks with referee Courtney Kirkland #61 during the first quarter against the Brooklyn Nets at Rocket Arena on October 24, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. However, they may have gotten some help from the referees in completing the comeback. Based on the NBA’s Last Two Minute Report , the Cavs were the beneficiaries of two missed calls at the end of regulation and overtime that assisted in the victory. The first incorrect call came at the end of regulation. The league says that Anthony Edwards should’ve been awarded free throws on a drive to the basket in the final seconds of regulation. Harden helped from the corner and reached in on the drive, but there’s little to suggest a foul should’ve been called. Maybe a different angle would lead you to believe otherwise. Edwards did throw his palms up in frustration when he saw a foul wasn’t called, so maybe there was some contact there. If this was called according to the report, the Cavs would’ve likely needed to make a basket to tie or win the game in the final 4.2 seconds of regulation. The whistle shouldn’t have blown, and play should’ve been allowed to continue. The closing seconds could’ve played out differently if this wasn’t called a foul. The Cavs earned a hard-fought victory on Monday. These two missed calls don’t take away from that, but Cleveland is fortunate that these decisions went in their favor.

item.title: Game Thread: Please keep the World Series going, Rays
item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 26: Chandler Simpson #14 and Richie Palacios #1 of the Tampa Bay Rays look on from the dugout during the ninth inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game three of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field on October 26, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images I don’t want the Rays to win the World Series. I didn’t want them to win before Game 1, and I ESPECIALLY don’t want them to win it now that they’re down three games to none, because I don’t want any team other than the 2004 Red Sox to ever win after being down three games to none ever again. This is very important to me. Having said that, my God, Rays, please win tonight. There are few more depressing days than the first few days after the baseball season ends, when the rhythm that has dictated your life since late March suddenly disappears. You don’t notice its absence on the first day after the series. Maybe you don’t notice it on the second day, either. But that third day is brutal. The third day brings that realization that the foreseeable future is dark and cold and has nothing for you at 7:10 PM on a Tuesday night. item.description: The Dante Moore era at Oregon appears to be over. Same for Drew Mehringer, just more conclusively so. item.description: EAST LANSING — Since her arrival in the Michigan State women's basketball program, Theryn Hallock has been used to being on the court. From finding a role as a freshman in the 2022-23 season, to being the Big Ten's top reserve as a sophomore, Hallock found a way to use her physical skills to help the Spartans have success. But that wasn't the case last season for the guard. A foot injury limited Hallock to just eight games last season, forcing her to view things from a different perspective. And now that Hallock is back for one last season, she hopes to use that new perspective gained a year ago from watching to help the Spartans this winter. "It's been great (being back)," Hallock said during the Spartans' media day Tuesday, Oct. 27. "I've been itching to get back out there. I hated being hurt but I also think it was a blessing in disguise. I learned a lot about myself, the coaches, the team and what I could bring when I come back. For the first time I had to be selfish and put myself first to get my body and mind right. I'm excited for people to see who I am coming back out there and what I'm bringing to the team." The return of Hallock for a fifth season is a big boost for a Spartan squad that features nine newcomers. She is one of the most experienced players on the roster with 100 career games under her belt and has averaged double-digits scoring each of the last three seasons while being part of NCAA tournament squads. Hallock earned postseason Big Ten recognition both as a sophomore and junior and is closing in on reaching 1,000 career points. According to Nielsen Media, by way of FOX Sports, Game 1 that saw the Brewers win 3-2 averaged 11,506,000 viewers. That’s down -6% compared to last year’s Game 1 between the Toronto Blue Jays and Los Angeles Dodgers, and down -19% from Game 1 of the 2024 World Series between the Dodgers and New York Yankees, but up over World Series Game 1’s in ’20 (+24.4%), ’21 (+6.4%), ’22 (+0.3%), and ’23 (+25.5%). Game 2, which saw the Brewers win 5-4, averaged 10,662,000 viewers. That outperformed three of last six World Series Game 2’s (’20, ‘21, ’23). item.title: 'A very sad day': Arteta despair as Arsenal stunned by Fleetwood
item.description: Fleetwood manager Matt Lawlor celebrates the League Cup victory over Arsenal (Darren Staples) Mikel Arteta said Arsenal's stunning League Cup defeat by fourth-tier Fleetwood was "a very sad day" as the Premier League champions suffered one of the most embarrassing results in their history. Arteta's side crashed out 5-3 on penalties in an incredible fourth round upset after the tie finished 1-1 in normal time. Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes had his penalty saved by Jay Lynch in the shoot-out and Conor Haughey scored Fleetwood's winner. Aaron Loupalo-Bi's first-half goal had put Fleetwood ahead before Viktor Gyokeres equalised after the interval. Arsenal's 16-year-old rising star Max Dowman was sent off for violent conduct in the closing stages. Arteta paid the price for prioritising Sunday's Premier League trip to Liverpool as his decision to make nine changes backfired spectacularly. The Gunners boss conceded Arsenal could have no complaints, admitting it was a painful moment in his reign. "First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood for going through the next round. The manner that they have done it, and for us a very sad day," Arteta said. "There is nothing to criticise the players for their attitude, their application. "The determination, you could see that was there from the start, even with 10 men. But we conceded a really poor goal to start with that gave them some momentum. "Obviously we have so much of the ball, so many chances, so many shots, and if you want the margins to be bigger than going to the penalties, you need to capitalise on that. And we didn't. "It's football, that's the beauty of this competition. It's a very sad day." Arsenal had moved level on points with Premier League leaders Manchester City after a 2-0 victory over Everton on Saturday. But instead of extending their run of 11 wins from their 13 previous games, Arteta's team returned to north London red-faced after a loss that ranks among the darkest days in the club's glittering history. "Zero problem attitude-wise. Otherwise, I would be here absolutely fuming. I'm sad, I think we are all sad. We have a massive responsibility to carry this badge in the best possible way," Arteta said. "You don't capitalise, then you cannot go through to the next round. Unfortunately, we are out." - 'I just can't believe it' - Although it looked a harsh decision to send off Dowman for aiming a kick towards Harrison Neal, Arteta was unimpressed with the 16-year-old, giving him a stern word as the midfielder trudged off. "Something that we discussed already before the match," Arteta said when asked what he told Dowman. "It's difficult to see on the cameras like that, so I prefer to watch it back properly and then I can assess the situation." item.description: Gattuso's Lazio enjoy stunning Serie A surge despite fan boycott The prospects of a successful season for Lazio did not look particularly bright after a 2025/2026 campaign that ended without a trophy or a place in European competition. Yet the team from the Italian capital have emerged as THE standout side in this season's Serie A despite having the WORST average attendance in the league! Tuesday's (27) win came not in Rome, but away at Sassuolo: 6–2, even with two missed penalties. It further underlines their impressive form in a season that began under challenging circumstances. Lazio moved to 25 points, ahead of Inter on 22, who have yet to play their ninth-round fixture. Gattuso's side—coming off his humiliating spell with the Italian national team—have the second-best attack, with 22 goals. They also boast the tightest defense, having conceded just seven. Why are home attendances so low? The strained relationship between a large section of the fans and Lazio president Claudio Lotito reached breaking point in January this year. 📸 Marco Rosi - SS Lazio - 2026 Getty Images Those supporters followed through on their promise not to renew their season tickets for games at the Olimpico after investment for the second half of last season fell short of expectations. The businessman and Italian senator has been unpopular with the Biancocelesti 's most passionate supporters since taking ownership of the club in 2004. He began curbing some of the control the ultras exercised over tickets and official club merchandise. Lotito has been suspended for his involvement in Calciopoli—the biggest match-fixing and corruption scandal in Italian football—for breaching COVID-19 regulations, and for violating rules on third-party ownership of players. He has also faced fierce criticism for downplaying (and denying) incidents of racism, as well as making disparaging comments about smaller clubs. The 69-year-old businessman has defended himself by pointing out, for example, that Lazio have won six trophies since his arrival, that he presented plans for the new Flaminio stadium and worked to complete the club's training center. But none of that has stopped the ongoing boycott, which has hit the club's finances hard this season. Lazio's average home attendance in this season's Serie A is just 9,515 at a stadium with a capacity of 70,634. Meanwhile, rivals Roma, who also play their home games at the Olimpico, have been drawing around 67,024 fans. It is a striking contrast, given that both teams are enjoying excellent campaigns. Monza have the second-lowest attendance: 10,124. But their stadium, the Brianteo, holds only 17,000. So far, Lazio's only disappointment in 2026/2027 has been their first-round exit from the Coppa Italia. That "helped" make their fixture list even lighter. item.title: Arteta defends Arsenal players’ attitude after shock Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood
item.description: Arteta defends Arsenal players’ attitude after shock Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood Mikel Arteta refused to criticise his players’ attitude after Arsenal’s shock Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood Town, insisting the defeat had nothing to do with a lack of effort or application. The Premier League champions were knocked out on penalties by the League Two side after a 1-1 draw, with Arteta instead pointing to their inability to take their chances. “First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood for going through to the next round and the manner they’ve done it, the atmosphere they have created,” Arteta said. “It’s a really sad day for us. I cannot fault the attitude of the players at all. I haven’t seen anyone not doing what is required at this level. “We had so much of the ball, so many chances, so many shots, and if you want the margin to be bigger than going to penalties, you have to capitalise on that and we didn’t.” Youngster Max Dowman was sent off late on in the tie but Arteta says he will need to watch the incident back before making a proper assessment. “It’s difficult to see, so I prefer to watch it back properly and then I can assess the situation,” he said. Asked if the 16-year-old can learn from the situation, Arteta said: “Yeah, we’ll learn from everything.” The Arsenal boss was adamant the defeat had nothing to do with a lack of commitment from his players, despite the disappointment of exiting the competition against lower-league opposition. “Attitude-wise, I have zero complaints, otherwise I would be absolutely fuming,” Arteta said. “I’m sad, I think we are all sad. We have a massive responsibility to carry this badge in the best possible way. “It was nothing to do with effort or application or determination to go and win it, but we lacked other things to create a much bigger margin that, with what we’ve produced, should have been shown in the scoreline.”

item.title: LeBron James’ Philadelphia Experiment Is Already Getting Complicated
item.description: Photo by: Bill Streicher LeBron James’ move to Philadelphia was supposed to give the 76ers another superstar capable of helping them compete for an NBA championship. However, just days into the 2026-27 season, the experiment is already facing an unexpected challenge. Philadelphia has started the season with plenty of excitement surrounding its new roster, but injuries and frontcourt concerns are creating questions about how the team will manage its rotation. Most notably, James has already been forced into a role that he never expected to play regularly at this stage of his career. LeBron James Faces an Unexpected Challenge During Philadelphia’s matchup against the Detroit Pistons on Sunday, James started at center because Joel Embiid and several other frontcourt options were unavailable. The 41-year-old finished with 18 points and five assists, but the 76ers suffered a 106-93 defeat. The loss exposed Philadelphia’s problems on the boards. Detroit outrebounded the 76ers 54-37 and scored 24 second chance points, demonstrating how difficult it can be for the team to replace its traditional big men. James has the versatility to play multiple positions, but he made it clear that becoming a full-time center is not part of his plans. “We got an MVP over there,” James said, referring to Embiid. He explained that playing center could be an option when necessary, but he does not expect it to become a permanent responsibility. That creates an important challenge for head coach Nick Nurse. Philadelphia needs to keep its roster healthy while finding reliable minutes behind Embiid. Can Philadelphia Make This Experiment Work? The 76ers still have plenty of talent. James joins a group featuring Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and promising young guard VJ Edgecombe, giving Philadelphia multiple options offensively. However, having star power does not automatically solve every problem. The team must establish chemistry, find a dependable backup center and determine how to distribute responsibilities without putting unnecessary physical demands on James. The early season remains young, so there is no reason to panic just yet. Still, Philadelphia’s championship hopes could depend on how quickly it addresses these issues. James has spent more than two decades adapting his game to different situations. Now, the biggest question is whether Philadelphia can build the right system around him before its early problems become a season-long concern.
